items.headline: Alphabet's record one-day drop pulls the Nasdaq down about 1.4% Thursday
items.note: The S&P 500 and Dow each slipped roughly 0.3%. Alphabet fell about 12% after third-quarter sales missed estimates, the worst day in its history by Yahoo Finance's account, erasing roughly $500 billion in value. Software and AI-linked names sold off in sympathy.

items.headline: Alphabet's miss revives worries about when AI spending pays off
items.note: Investors focused on weak sales and free cash flow against heavy AI spending. Microsoft beat expectations on sales and profit and held up better than Alphabet. Big Tech's AI budgets set how much these firms hire for ML roles.

items.headline: Amazon's free cash flow turns to a $42.4B outflow as it holds 2026 capex at $220B
items.note: Amazon fell about 4% on Thursday after reporting; it had dropped about 10% after hours before trimming losses. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was an outflow versus a $14.8B inflow a year earlier.

items.headline: Economy grew at a 3.4% pace in Q3, but inflation is still running hot
items.note: Initial GDP beat the 3.1% expected, helping small caps rally. September PCE inflation rose 3.6% from a year earlier (core 3.1%). Strong growth plus high inflation keeps a December Fed hike in play, per reports.

items.headline: Intel plunges roughly 17-20% on a weak revenue outlook
items.note: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15-16B versus about $17B expected. It is a reminder that chip stocks are priced on forward guidance, not only past results.

items.headline: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for about $17B
items.note: The deal is $65 per share, a 26% premium to Instacart's Oct. 22 close, at least 75% in cash. DoorDash pitches pairing delivery with Instacart's grocery tech plus both firms' advertising and AI tools; both are big data and ML employers.

items.headline: Tech layoffs top roughly 196,000 in 2026, but AI and data roles keep hiring
items.note: TrueUp's count was about 196,000 as of Oct. 23; other trackers show lower totals. Reports say employers are cutting generalist and entry-level roles while still hiring for AI/ML and data engineering, so internship applications should stress specific skills.

items.headline: Microsoft recorded about $10B of revenue from OpenAI last quarter
items.note: TechCrunch says that is nearly 11% of Microsoft's $92.3B quarter. It shows how much of the AI boom rests on a few big customer relationships.

items.headline: Anthropic launches 'Smart Reports' to show what a company's AI spending buys
items.note: The tools show what teams produced, what it cost and where workflows broke down. Measuring AI's return on investment is becoming a real analytics job.

learn.explain: PCE (personal consumption expenditures) is a price index published by the government that tracks what households pay for goods and services. The Fed prefers it to CPI because it adjusts as people switch to cheaper products and covers more spending. Core PCE leaves out food and energy, which swing a lot. The Fed's usual goal is about 2% a year. Today's report showed September PCE up 3.6% from a year earlier, with core at 3.1%, well above that goal.
learn.try: Look up the Fed's 2% target and compare it with core PCE over the past year.

learned: Capital spending (capex) and free cash flow
